_comment: Collected 2026-11-10 from HND Bayern 'Statistik' pages (hnd.bayern.de/pegel/.../statistik) and, for Linz, computed directly from the real eHYD daily CSV (no HND-equivalent page exists for Austria). For validation and flood-event counting only (Phase 5a decision 4) -- NOT the source of the actual daily series used in the app, which comes from the GKD/eHYD CSV downloads processed in Phase 5b. Some HND statistik pages return a recent-window top-5 (e.g. Passau's visible table starts in 2016 despite including 2013/2002/1981 entries) rather than a true all-time top-5; where a well-documented older flood (e.g. 1954) is known to be missing from a station's own digitized top-5, that is noted explicitly rather than silently added.

stations.name: Passau / Donau
stations.meldestufenNote: Not shown on the statistik page itself; not separately collected for this gauge (Pegelonline/WSV-operated, may be federally managed rather than through HND's Bavarian Meldestufen system).
stations.notes: 1954 flood (1220 cm, ~10/11 July 1954, independently confirmed via undine.bafg.de and hochwasser-passau.de -- see Phase 5a report) does NOT appear in this gauge's own digitized top-5, which otherwise matches real 2013/2002/2024 figures closely. 2013-06-03 1290 cm matches the user-supplied 12.89 m almost exactly (1 cm rounding). 2024-06-04 998 cm = 9.98 m, i.e. just under 10 m, not over 10 m as recalled.

stations.name: Passau Ilzstadt / Donau (reference only -- NOT used; see Phase 5a decision)
stations.notes: 1.45 km further downstream than 10091008, catchment 76,642 km2 (includes Inn + Ilz, vs 10091008's 49,738 km2 Danube-only). Pegelonline's own HHW field for this station read '1279 cm, 10.07.1954' in one fetch -- this conflicts with the independently verified 1954 value of 1220 cm at the main Passau gauge, and is flagged here as unresolved/unverified rather than used for anything. The app uses 10091008 (GKD's official 'Passau / Donau', = Pegelonline 'PASSAU DONAU') per the explicit instruction, not this station.

stations.name: Linz / Donau
stations.sourceUrl: https://ehyd.gv.at/services/MessstellenExtraData/owf?id=207068&file=2 (computed directly from the real daily CSV, 1921-01-01 to 2024-01-01)
stations.meldestufenNote: eHYD/Austria has no Meldestufen-equivalent field exposed in this export; not collected.

top5.date: 1954 (year max; exact date not extracted in this pass)

stations.notes: Computed from real data, not a web table -- see Phase 5a report. At Linz, 1954 (954 cm) is HIGHER than 2013 (888 cm), the reverse ranking from Passau -- a genuine real difference between the two gauges, not an error. Old hand-typed LINZ_DANUBE_HISTORICAL values (useAustriaFloodData.ts: 1954=8.9m, 2002=9.05m, 2013=9.28m) are all wrong; real values are 9.54 m, 8.06 m, 8.88 m respectively.

stations.name: Neu-Ulm / Donau
stations.top5_discharge_m3s_NOTE: Search returned a discharge (Abfluss) extremes table, not water level -- re-check the level statistik directly when downloading.
stations.notes: Ulm itself is in Baden-Württemberg, outside GKD Bayern's network -- Neu-Ulm (Bavaria side) is the real equivalent, used here in place of the app's generic 'Ulm' label.

stations.name: Ingolstadt Luitpoldstraße / Donau
stations.notes: 2024 is the actual #1 record at this gauge, unlike Passau/Deggendorf/Schwabelweis where 2013 remains highest -- genuine spatial variation along the Danube, not an error.

stations.name: Schwabelweis / Donau
stations.notes: Unlike Passau's statistik page, 1954 DOES appear here (tied 5th, 656 cm, 1954-07-13) -- this gauge's digitized record goes back further. 'Schwabelweis' is GKD/HND's name for what the app currently labels 'Regensburg'.

stations.name: Deggendorf / Donau
stations.notes: Three-way tie at 745 cm for 2nd-4th (2024, 2002, 1999) as reported by the search summary -- worth re-verifying exact cm precision directly from the page when downloading, a tie this exact across 3 different decades is slightly unusual.

stations.name: Donauwörth / Donau
stations.notes: Confirmed on the Danube, not the Lech (per Phase 5a decision) -- moved from the app's Lech list to the Danube list. Statistik top-5/Meldestufen not yet collected for this station; fetch alongside the others in Phase 5b.

stations.name: Rosenheim o.d. Mangfallmündung / Inn
stations.notes: A second, very similar 'Rosenheim u.d. Mangfallmündung' gauge (18002001, downstream of the same confluence) also exists with slightly different values (e.g. 2013 peak 468 cm there vs 511 cm here) -- 'o.d.' (upstream of Mangfall) is used here since it's the one with full Meldestufen confirmed.

stations.name: Braunau-Simbach KW / Inn (original app station -- EXCLUDED per Phase 5a decision)
stations.notes: Confirmed hydropower-company-operated (Verbund AG Wasserkraft Österreich), not LfU/WWA -- download/licence status for a third-party hydropower gauge was not pursued further since a real WWA Deggendorf alternative (Passau-Ingling, 18008008) was found on the same river, lower down, closer to the Danube confluence.

stations.name: Passau Ingling / Inn (replaces Braunau-Simbach KW)
stations.meldestufenNote: Only a single 'Meldebeginn 475 cm' figure found, not broken into M1-M4 separately -- re-check the live page directly in Phase 5b.
stations.notes: Government-operated (WWA Deggendorf), at the very mouth of the Inn (river km 3.10, just above the Danube confluence at Passau) -- the most representative 'full Inn' gauge available, and a real government station rather than a hydropower company's. This is a DIFFERENT physical location from Braunau (further upstream, at the Austria border) -- flagged clearly since the app's existing 'Braunau' label/coordinates would need to move or be relabeled, a decision left to Phase 5b's geoData.ts update.

stations.name: München / Isar
stations.notes: Matches the existing hand-typed STATION_IDS['München'] = '16005701' in useFloodData.ts exactly -- already the correct site number, just never had real data pulled from it.

stations.name: Landshut Birket / Isar
stations.notes: Only 3 of 5 top entries captured in this pass -- re-check directly in Phase 5b. 'Landshut Birket', not 'Landshut Flutmulde' (16007106), per the explicit decision.

stations.name: Augsburg u. d. Wertachmündung / Lech
stations.notes: Only 3 of 5 top entries captured in this pass. 2013 is notably NOT in this short list (Lech flooding was much less severe than Danube/Isar/Inn that year) -- consistent with real 2013 meteorology being Danube/Inn-centered. This is the LOWEST (most downstream) state-operated gauge on the Lech -- confirmed via two independent checks (WWA Donauwörth's own Lech Gewässerportrait page, and the Augsburg gauge's own 'nearby stations' list) that no further-downstream Lech gauge exists in the Bavarian state network; Donauwörth itself is on the Danube, not the Lech.

stations.name: Stock / Chiemsee
stations.lowest_years_NOTE: Not resolved via web search in this pass -- the lowest-years ranking (needed for the professor's 2022-2023 record-low question) will be computed directly from the real downloaded daily CSV in Phase 5b instead of guessed from a secondary source.
stations.notes: Record period shown as 1907-2025 for the extremes table, but the station's own 'observation period since 2010' note (from a separate Stammdaten search) suggests the current physical instrument/series may only start 2010, with earlier values carried forward from a predecessor gauge at the same site -- verify the real download's actual start date directly.

stations.name: Starnberg / Starnberger See
stations.notes: Record period 1907-2025 for extremes, 1907-2022 for main values.
